newsitem.title: USA: John Hinckley petitions to be allowed family visits.
newsitem.headline: John Hinckley petitions to be allowed family visits.

text.p: John Hinckley Jr., confined to a mental hospital after shooting then-President Ronald Reagan in 1981, petitioned again on Monday to be allowed to make unescorted visits to see his parents, federal prosecutors said.
"He wants his conditions of confinement to be loosened," said Harry Benner, a spokesman for the U.S. attorney's office, which is handling the case. "He wants to be able to move around more freely."
Hinckley has been confined at the St. Elizabeth's mental hospital in Washington since 1982 when he was acquitted by reason of insanity on charges of shooting Reagan and three others.
Reagan and two police guards recovered fully from the attack, but Reagan press secretary James Brady was left critically wounded.
U.S. District Court Judge June Green heard the first of several days of arguments in which the government will contend Hinckley is not fit to make such parental visits.

It would be at least the fourth attempt by Hinckley's lawyers to allow him to make visits to his parents. Prosecutors and hospital officials have previously opposed the requests. Over the last decade Hinckley has been allowed to leave the hospital for court appearances only.
